This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum
 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum)
This appeal is by the claimants questioning the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.104/2016.

The Tribunal in absence of medical evidence to establish that cause of death was on account NC: 2024:KHC-K:9546 of head injury sustained in a road traffic accident dated 09.04.2015, has declined to award compensation under the head of loss of dependency and conventional heads.
The claim petition is partly allowed by awarding medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,13,000/-.
The said judgment is under challenge.

2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants and learned counsel appearing for respondent - insurance company.
3.
The original claimant Bhimappa S/o Narasappa filed a claim petition for having sustained grievous head injury in a road traffic accident dated 09.04.2015.

Pending consideration of the claim petition, Bhimappa, who had sustained grievous head injury died and therefore, widow, two minor children and parents were permitted to come record and prosecute the claim petition to enable them Bhimappa S/O Narasappa Since Deceased ... vs Usman Sab S/O Nabi Sab And Anr

on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50214021/
2 to seek compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

The claimants except producing wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills and NC: 2024:KHC-K:9546 medical prescriptions,
failed to produce medical evidence to establish that death of Bhimappa was on account of head injury sustained in a road traffic accident dated 09.04.2015.
4. The medical records, particularly Ex.P8, clearly establish that Bhimappa sustained a serious head injury in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.05.2015.
Following the accident, he was initially admitted to KIMS Hospital but was subsequently referred to Omni Hospital, Hyderabad, for advanced treatment.
At Omni Hospital, Hyderabad, Bhimappa received treatment for a period of four days.
However, upon the request of his family, he was discharged from the hospital.
Despite undergoing treatment, Bhimappa succumbed to his injuries on 30.07.2017, nearly two years after the accident.
The discharge card, in conjunction with the wound certificate, unequivocally reveals the severity of Bhimappa's head injury.
Upon his admission to Omni Hospital, Hyderabad, Bhimappa exhibited signs of critical trauma.
He was drowsy, a condition attributed to the head injury he had sustained.
The discharge card further records that he had laceration injuries, blood oozing from his right ear, and an inability to respond to verbal commands.

Additionally, the CT scan results highlighted significant findings,
including a hyperdense area in the left sylvian cistern, subarachnoid hemorrhage, a mixed dense area in the left temporal region, and cerebral contusion.
These findings underscore the grave nature of the injuries suffered by Bhimappa in the road traffic accident.

6. Despite the availability of these critical pieces of medical evidence, the claimants, who have lost their primary breadwinner, have not examined the treating doctors to establish a direct causal link between the head injury sustained in the accident on 09.05.2015 and Bhimappa's subsequent death on 30.07.2017.

The absence of such corroborative medical testimony has left a NC:
2024:KHC-K:9546 crucial gap in the evidence needed to substantiate their claim.
7.
After meticulous examination of the discharge card and the wound certificate, this Court is of the opinion that the matter requires reconsideration.

The claimants should be afforded an opportunity to lead additional medical evidence to establish the direct nexus between the fatal head injury sustained in the road traffic accident and Bhimappa's eventual death.
The fact that Bhimappa was a young man, merely 25 years of age, at the time of the accident, adds weight to the probability of such a connection.
Furthermore, the circumstances highlight the importance of re-evaluating the claim with additional medical evidence.
8. It is also pertinent to note that the postmortem report does not provide conclusive assistance to the claimants, as the opinion therein remains reserved.

The claim petition was filed by the widow,
who was also 25 years old at the time and is left with two minor children NC: 2024:KHC-K:9546 and elderly in-laws to care for.
In the interest of justice and considering the profound impact on the family, this Court finds it appropriate to remit the matter back to the Tribunal.

The appellants/claimants are granted the liberty to examine the treating doctors or any other relevant Bhimappa S/O Narasappa Since Deceased ... vs Usman Sab S/O Nabi Sab And Anr on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50214021/
3 medical experts to substantiate their claim and prove that Bhimappa's death was directly linked to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
This approach ensures that the case is comprehensively assessed and justice is rendered to the affected family.

9. For the foregoing reasons, this Court passes the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.104/2016 is hereby set aside.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9546 c) The matter is remitted back to Tribunal to enable the appellants/claimants to lead further evidence.
d) The respondent - insurance company shall forthwith deposit the medical expenses awarded by the Tribunal with 6% interest from the date of claim petition till its realization.

e) Since parties are represented by their respective counsels, without expecting any further notice,
shall appear before the Tribunal on 30.12.2024.
f) Registry is directed to transmit the Trial Court records forthwith.

Sd/-
